endorsements.quote: For patients and caregivers, ethical use requires plain-language communication, explicit signaling of uncertainty, and safeguards against over-reliance.
Health-care systems must therefore establish mechanisms for ongoing evaluation, feedback, and revision of LLM deployment, recognizing that ethical risks may emerge, intensify, or transform over time.

unlisted_practices: Define institutional responsibility for how LLM outputs are generated, validated, and monitored within clinical and informational workflows.
Design LLM systems to be role-sensitive, treating clinician and patient roles differently in authority, expertise, and exposure to harm.
Design LLM systems for clinicians to support professional accountability, auditability, and calibrated reliance without increasing cognitive burden.
Adopt literacy-sensitive interfaces, adaptive explanatory strategies, and targeted support for underserved populations when deploying LLMs.
Treat ethical oversight of LLM adoption as a continuous governance process rather than a one-time pre-deployment assessment.
Clarify responsibility when AI-mediated information influences communication or decision-making.

screen.reason: This is a normative ethical analysis/framework paper discussing the ethical shifts, risks, and governance recommendations (continuous oversight, institutional accountability) for adopting large language models in healthcare.
